pr_title: perf: Added optimizer rules for `is_null().all()` and similar expressions to use `null_count()`
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/17605.

Added rules:

- is_null().all() -> null_count() == len()
- is_null().any() -> null_count() > 0
- is_not_null().all() -> null_count() == 0
- is_not_null().any() -> null_count() < len()
- is_null().sum() -> null_count()
- is_not_null().sum() -> len() - null_count()
- drop_nulls().len() -> len() - null_count()
- drop_nulls().count() -> len() - null_count()

Thanks.

issue_context.title: Optimize `is_null().any()` and similar operations that can be written in terms of null count
issue_context.body:
### Description

In Polars the null count of a series is cached, so it can be retrieved for free. Some operations can be re-written during optimization to be much more efficient using this.

### Example
```python
import polars as pl
import timeit

lf = pl.select(pl.repeat(None, 10_000_000, dtype=pl.Int8)).lazy()

q = lf.select(pl.first().is_null().any()).collect
t = timeit.timeit(q, number=10_000)
print("is_null().any() :: ", t)

q = lf.select(pl.first().null_count() > 0).collect
t = timeit.timeit(q, number=10_000)
print("null_count() > 0 :: ", t)
```

Output
```python
is_null().any() ::  1.7241754580754787
null_count() > 0 ::  0.04942204221151769
```

It's probably also quite common for users to write code like this (e.g. to a human `is_not_null().any()` is a little easier to understand than `len() > null_count()`).

Not an exhaustive list, but here's some examples that can be re-written:
* `is_null().all()` -> `null_count() == len()`
* `is_null().any()` -> `null_count() > 0`
* `is_not_null().all()` -> `null_count() == 0`
* `is_not_null().any()` -> `len() > null_count()`
* `is_null().sum()` -> `null_count()`
* `is_not_null().sum()` -> `len() - null_count()`
* `drop_nulls().len()` -> `len() - null_count()`
* `drop_nulls().count()` -> `len() - null_count()`

This might be a little advanced for a first issue, but it's a very good opportunity to learn a bit about how Polars' optimizers work. The starting point is probably here - https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-plan/src/plans/optimizer/simplify_functions.rs.
